title: Abduction with two checks
description: The Abduction example with both tests moved out of the abstraction: one check solver looks for a witness that the hypotheses are consistent with the theory, a second one for a counterexample to the entailment. A failed witness check is refined with its unsat core (the hypotheses that contradict the theory), a counterexample through relevant/1. Compare with Abduction, which keeps the consistency witness inside the abstraction.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The theory, the hypotheses and the manifestations. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Why does the car not start? A theory in clause form:
% pos(C,A): atom A occurs in clause C, neg(C,A): its negation does.
neg(1,flat).    pos(1,nostart).                   % a flat battery: no start
neg(2,flat).    pos(2,dim).                       % a flat battery: dim lights
neg(3,empty).   pos(3,nostart).                   % an empty tank: no start
neg(4,starter). pos(4,nostart).                   % a broken starter: no start
neg(5,plugs).   neg(5,damp). pos(5,nostart).      % fouled plugs in a damp engine: no start
neg(6,cold).    pos(6,flat). pos(6,damp).         % a cold night: flat battery or damp engine
neg(7,lights).  pos(7,flat).                      % lights left on: flat battery
neg(8,rain).    pos(8,damp).                      % rain: damp engine
pos(9,gauge).                                     % the fuel gauge shows fuel
neg(10,gauge).  neg(10,empty).                    % ... so the tank is not empty
clause(C) :- pos(C,_).
clause(C) :- neg(C,_).
atom(A) :- pos(_,A).
atom(A) :- neg(_,A).
% What may be assumed, and what has to be explained.
hypothesis(flat; empty; starter; plugs; cold; lights; rain).
manifestation(nostart).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): any set of at most k hypotheses.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k hypotheses. Nothing else: both tests are left to the checks.
{ assume(H) : hypothesis(H) } k.
#show assume/1.
% 'always' is true in every candidate. The check blames it when a counterexample does
% not depend on the candidate: then no candidate is a solution, and the clause "always
% must change" ends the search.
{ always }.
:- not always.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the assumed hypotheses.

fragments.name: consistent
fragments.description: The first check (solver C1): a witness that theory and hypotheses are consistent.
fragments.text:
% A witness, not a counterexample: a model of the theory in which the assumed
% hypotheses hold. If there is none, the hypotheses contradict the theory, and the
% unsat core names the hypotheses that are to blame.
{ w(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not w(A) : pos(C,A); w(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not w(H).
#show w/1.

fragments.name: entails
fragments.description: The second check (solver C2): a model in which a manifestation is false.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a model of the theory and the assumed hypotheses in which some
% manifestation is false. Then the hypotheses do not entail the manifestations.
{ m(A) } :- atom(A).
:- clause(C), not m(A) : pos(C,A); m(A) : neg(C,A).
:- assume(H), not m(H).
:- m(A) : manifestation(A).
#show m/1.

% The model refutes every set of hypotheses that are all true in it. So a hypothesis
% that is false in the model has to be assumed.
relevant(assume(H)) :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
% If all hypotheses are true in the model, nothing explains the manifestations: blame
% the atom that is always true.
missing :- hypothesis(H), not m(H).
relevant(always) :- not missing.

loop.text:
solver A  = shared + abstraction
solver C1 = shared + consistent
solver C2 = shared + entails       options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G1 = A -> C1 via shared + glue
link   G2 = A -> C2 via shared + glue

# Two checks of two kinds. C1 looks for a witness (a model that shows the hypotheses
# are consistent with the theory): no witness, no solution, and the unsat core of the
# failed solve is the refinement. C2 looks for a counterexample (a model in which a
# manifestation is false) and refines through relevant/1.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        if not C1.solve(assume G1(M)):
            reject M with G1.core(C1)
        else:
            X = C2.solve(assume G2(M))
            if X: reject M with G2.clause(M, X)

library.summary: Propositional abduction with a witness check (refined by unsat cores) and a counterexample check (7 hypotheses, k = 2, 17 solutions).
